items.title: COVID-19: 5G broadband conspiracy 'a hoax with no technical basis'
items.snippet_en: The ITU, the UN's agency for information and communication technologies, confirmed that 5G is not responsible for the spread of COVID-19, calling the conspiracy a 'hoax with no technical basis'.

items.title: Clearing up the myths around 5G and the coronavirus
items.snippet_en: Ofcom states there is no scientific basis or credible evidence for claims linking 5G to the spread of coronavirus.

items.title: DHS to advise telecom firms on preventing 5G cell tower attacks linked to coronavirus conspiracy theories
items.snippet_en: Eric van Rongen of ICNIRP stated it's physically impossible for electromagnetic fields to transfer viruses, and there's no scientific basis for 5G compromising the immune system. The WHO also stated viruses cannot travel via radio waves.

items.title: 5G and coronavirus (COVID-19)
items.snippet_en: The UK government states there is no evidence of a link between 5G and coronavirus, and that viruses cannot travel on radio waves or mobile networks. The WHO also supports this.

items.title: Are 5G Networks Spreading the Coronavirus?
items.snippet_en: This article debunks the myth, citing ICNIRP and FEMA, both stating that 5G does not cause COVID-19. The WHO is also cited as stating viruses cannot travel via radio waves.
The WHO has stated that viruses cannot travel via radio waves or mobile networks, and that COVID-19 is appearing in countries without advanced wireless systems.
